title: Last-Level Cache Side-Channel Attacks Are Feasible in the Modern Public Cloud
problem: Last-level cache side-channel attacks have been demonstrated only in controlled, quiescent environments. It remains unclear whether such attacks are practical in production cloud environments where multi-tenant noise masks side-channel signals and attacker execution time is severely limited, especially in FaaS workloads.
motivation: Establishing the real-world feasibility of cache side-channel attacks in cloud is critical for understanding cloud security risks and designing appropriate defenses against information leakage.
method: The paper develops and demonstrates practical LLC side-channel attack techniques that operate effectively in production cloud environments despite multi-tenant interference and tight execution time windows. The techniques likely employ optimized cache-based timing observations or prime-and-probe variants adapted to tolerate cloud noise.
key_novelty: This work provides the first practical evidence that LLC side-channel attacks remain feasible in production cloud environments, contradicting the assumption that multi-tenancy and timing constraints provide sufficient protection.
contributions: Demonstrates LLC side-channel attacks succeed in production cloud despite multi-tenant noise
Develops attack techniques optimized for FaaS time constraints and cloud interference patterns
Establishes practical threat model for cache-based information leakage in cloud
Provides security implications and baseline for cloud provider defenses

metrics.other: attack success rate, information leakage capacity
